title: Kenyan Honey Glazed Chicken
community: Popular in urban Kenyan households and restaurants
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Honey Glazed Chicken — chicken pieces marinated in a balance of honey, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and lemon, then grilled or roasted until the glaze caramelises into a sticky, deeply flavourful golden coating. Sweet, savoury, and completely irresistible.
longDesc: Honey glazed chicken has become a fixture in Kenyan urban restaurants and home kitchens — the combination of local honey with garlic, ginger, and lemon juice creates a glaze that caramelises into something deeply flavourful during grilling. It is sweet enough to be a crowd-pleaser for all ages while remaining complex enough for sophisticated palates.
steps: Mix honey, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, lemon juice, oil, paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper into a marinade.
Coat the chicken thoroughly. Marinate for 1 hour minimum.
Grill method: cook over medium charcoal or gas for 12—15 minutes per side. Baste with remaining marinade every 5 minutes during the last 15 minutes.
Oven method: roast at 200°C for 30—35 minutes, basting every 10 minutes.
The glaze is ready when it is sticky, caramelised, and deeply golden — watch carefully in the last 5 minutes to prevent burning.
Rest 5 minutes, garnish with coriander, and serve.
chefTips: Add the honey glaze basting only in the last 15 minutes of cooking — honey burns quickly over high heat.
The higher the honey content, the faster the glaze caramelises — watch carefully.
A little soy sauce adds umami depth and balances the sweetness.
commonMistakes: Basting with honey glaze from the start — it burns long before the chicken is cooked.
Not scoring the chicken — the glaze stays on the surface.

faqs.q: Can I use agave or maple syrup instead of honey?
faqs.a: Yes — both work well. Agave gives a lighter sweetness; maple syrup adds a slightly caramel depth that works beautifully with the spices.

cookingScience: Honey contains simple sugars (fructose and glucose) that caramelise rapidly at relatively low temperatures (around 160°C). This is why honey-glazed foods develop their characteristic deep golden colour and sticky texture during cooking, and why basting should only begin in the final cooking phase.
sustainabilityTips: Use local Kenyan honey — supporting small-scale beekeepers and biodiversity.
reheating: Reheat in oven at 180°C for 8—10 minutes.
healthBenefits: Honey provides natural antioxidants and antimicrobial compounds.
Garlic and ginger add anti-inflammatory benefits.
culturalNote: Honey glazed chicken represents the modern Kenyan kitchen — drawing on local ingredients like Kenyan honey while embracing flavour combinations that have become part of the urban culinary identity.
regionalVariations: Chilli honey chicken — sweet heat combination.
